newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-OFF-FORM PARMA RELY ON HISTORY AGAINST FIORENTINA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-OFF-FORM PARMA RELY ON HISTORY AGAINST FIORENTINA.

text.p: Off-form Parma hope to maintain a winning record in home league ties against Fiorentina stretching back 65 years when the two sides meet in Parma on Sunday night.
Fiorentina last beat Parma away in February 1931, a statistic which owes much to the fact that Parma achieved promotion to Serie A only in 1990.
Parma, already out of both the UEFA and Italian Cups, have lost to Lazio, Perugia and Internazionale in three of their last four league outings.
But such is the cramped nature of the early-season Serie A positions that Parma are still only four points behind leaders Juventus and Inter.
The poor start by Parma, one of Italy's biggest mid-summer spenders, has inevitably led to speculation about coach Carlo Ancelotti, who is in his first year with the club.
But Parma president Stefano Tanzi this week denied the club had considered sacking the coach.
"At the end of the day we're only four points behind the leaders and we've lost nothing yet. All we need is one good result," Tanzi said.
Ancelotti may drop goalkeeper Luca Bucci and bring in 18-year-old Gianluigi Buffon, who did well in a nine-match Serie A run last season.
Parma will field a three-man attack of Argentine Hernan Crespo, Gianfranco Zola and Enrico Chiesa, with Frenchman Daniel Bravo, Argentine Nestor Sensini and Dino Baggio in midfield.
Parma are sure to find opponents Fiorentina in confident mood.
Fiorentina reached the last eight of the European Cup Winners' Cup at the expense of Sparta Prague on Thursday, four days after beating AC Milan 1-0 in the Italian league.

Fiorentina appear to have come out of the Prague tie with no injury problems and are likely to field their strongest side, featuring Argentine Gabriel Batistuta and Brazilian Oliveira in attack, with Swede Stefan Schwarz and Portugal's Rui Costa in midfield.
